note.text:
Mark-up on cost: profit as a percentage of the cost price.
Selling price = cost price + mark-up; mark-up = cost × rate. Cost 8 000, mark-up 25%: profit 2 000, selling price 10 000.
Margin (mark-up on sales): profit as a percentage of the selling price: 2 000 ÷ 10 000 = 20%.
An invoice is built step by step:
gross amount (quantity × unit price) − trade discount = net commercial amount; + VAT (19.25% in Cameroon) = net to pay (total including tax).
Example: 40 000 − 10% discount (4 000) = 36 000; VAT 19.25% = 6 930; net to pay 42 930 FCFA.
Sale recorded: debit 411 Customers, credit 701 Sales (net commercial) and 443 VAT collected.

worked_example.problem: Goods cost {c} FCFA and the mark-up on cost is {m}%. Find the selling price and the margin on sales.
steps: Mark-up = {c} × {m}% = {c * m / 100} FCFA; selling price = {c} + {c * m / 100} = {c + c * m / 100} FCFA.
Margin on sales = {c * m / 100} ÷ {c + c * m / 100} × {100} = {roundTo(c * m / (c + c * m / 100), 0.01)}%.
worked_example.answer: Selling price {c + c * m / 100} FCFA; margin {roundTo(c * m / (c + c * m / 100), 0.01)}%

cards.idea: Selling price = cost + cost × mark-up rate.
Margin on sales = profit ÷ selling price × {100}.

check.prompt: Goods cost {c} FCFA and sell for {s} FCFA. What is the margin as a percentage of the selling price?

misconceptions.explain: That is the mark-up on cost; divide by the selling price.

cards.idea: Invoice: gross − discount = net commercial; + VAT ({19.25}%) = net to pay.

check.prompt: An invoice shows goods worth {g} FCFA with a {d}% trade discount, then VAT at 19.25%. What is the net to pay?

misconceptions.explain: Add the VAT (19.25%) to the net commercial amount.
Take off the trade discount first.

solution: Net commercial = {g} − {g * d / 100} = {g - g * d / 100} FCFA.
VAT = {g - g * d / 100} × {19.25}% = {roundTo((g - g * d / 100) * 0.1925, 1)}; net to pay = {answer} FCFA.
